content.summary: Guidance on anticoagulation in patients with cancer-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE). Evidence from randomized and cohort studies comparing LMWH, edoxaban, rivaroxaban and dalteparin is summarized, with attention to bleeding risk (particularly gastrointestinal) and recurrence risk.
recommendations: For patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) and cancer, particularly gastrointestinal cancer, continue low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for about 3–6 months.
LMWH is preferred for patients in whom oral treatment is unfeasible (problems with intake/absorption) or those with severe renal impairment.
In patients without gastrointestinal tumours and with low anticipated bleeding risk, choice between LMWH and DOACs (edoxaban or rivaroxaban) may be left to physician and patient preference.

Because of high recurrence risk, patients with cancer should receive indefinite anticoagulation after a first episode of VTE; however, once cancer is cured anticoagulation may be stopped case-by-case.

After the first 3–6 months, extended anticoagulation may continue with LMWH or transition to an oral anticoagulant; decision should be individualized considering cancer control, recurrence risk, bleeding risk and patient preference.

Venous filters are principally indicated when anticoagulation is impossible due to active hemorrhage or excessive bleeding risk; insertion should be considered carefully given high VTE recurrence risk in cancer.

evidence_summary.comparative_outcomes: Randomized/open-label pilot trials compared rivaroxaban vs dalteparin (n=406) and other trials compared edoxaban vs LMWH. Rivaroxaban showed decreased recurrent VTE risk (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.19–0.99) but higher major bleeding, largely gastrointestinal.
evidence_summary.bleeding_and_crnm_rates: 6-month cumulative major bleeding: rivaroxaban 6% (95% CI ~3–11%), dalteparin 4% (95% CI ~2–8%). Clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding: rivaroxaban 13% (95% CI ~9–19%), dalteparin 4% (95% CI ~2–9%). Reported HR for CRNM bleeds ~3.76 (95% CI 1.63–8.69).
evidence_summary.timing_of_bleeding_complications: Incidence higher in the first months of extended treatment with LMWH (up to ~12 months) then reached a plateau after six months.

risk_of_recurrence_and_score.cohort_validation: Risk of recurrence of PE in cancer assessed in a cohort of 543 patients and validated in independent set of 819 patients.
proposed_score_components: Tumour Node Metastasis (TNM) stage I or II (minus 1 point)
risk_of_recurrence_and_score.risk_categories: Score ≤0 = low risk (≈4.5% recurrence over 6 months). Score ≥1 = high risk (≈19% recurrence over 6 months).

practical_considerations.individualization: In absence of conclusive evidence, decision to continue LMWH vs change to vitamin K antagonists (VKA) or a NOAC should be made case-by-case, with periodic reassessment of risk-to-benefit.
practical_considerations.special_populations: Patients with gastrointestinal cancer have higher bleeding risk on DOACs and should be particularly considered for LMWH.
